## 49. člen

(1) The court shall impose a sentence on the perpetrator of a criminal offence within the limits prescribed by law for that offence, having regard to the gravity of the offence committed and the perpetrator's culpability.
(2) In doing so, the court shall take into account all circumstances that affect whether the sentence should be lesser or greater (mitigating and aggravating circumstances), in particular: the degree of the perpetrator's culpability, the motives from which the act was committed, the degree of endangerment or violation of the protected legal value, the circumstances in which the act was committed, the perpetrator's previous life, his personal and financial circumstances, his conduct after the commission of the act, in particular whether he has compensated for the damage caused by the criminal offence, and other circumstances relating to the perpetrator's personality and the expected effect of the sentence on the perpetrator's future life in the social environment.

(3) If the motive for the commission of the criminal offence was the victim's national, racial, religious or ethnic affiliation, his sex, colour, origin, financial status, education, social position, political or other conviction, disability, sexual orientation or any other personal circumstance, this shall be taken into account as an aggravating circumstance.
(4) In imposing a sentence on a perpetrator who has committed a criminal offence after having already been finally convicted or after having served the sentence or after it has become time-barred or after it has been remitted (recidivism), the court shall take into account in particular whether the previous act was of the same type as the new one, whether both acts were committed from the same motives, and how much time has elapsed since the previous conviction or since the served, remitted or time-barred sentence.

Mitigation of sentence

## 50. člen

The court may impose a sentence on the perpetrator below the limit prescribed by law or apply a milder type of sentence:
- if the law provides that the perpetrator may be punished more leniently;
- if it finds special mitigating circumstances that justify the imposition of a mitigated sentence.

Limits of mitigation of imprisonment sentence

## 51. člen

(1) Where the conditions for mitigation of sentence under the preceding article are met, the court shall mitigate it within the following limits:
1) if fifteen years of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to ten years of imprisonment;
2) if three or more years of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to one year of imprisonment;
3) if one year of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to three months of imprisonment;
4) if less than one year of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to one month of imprisonment;
5) if a sentence of imprisonment is prescribed for the criminal offence and no minimum sentence is specified, it may impose a fine instead of imprisonment.
(2) For a perpetrator who, under the law governing criminal procedure, admits guilt when first making a statement on the indictment in which mitigation of sentence is proposed for such a case, or admits it in an agreement with the state prosecutor, the court shall mitigate the sentence within the following limits:
1) if ten or more years of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to three years of imprisonment;
2) if three to ten years of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to three months of imprisonment;
3) if less than three years of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may mitigate it to one month of imprisonment;
4) if less than one year of imprisonment is prescribed as the minimum sentence for the criminal offence, it may impose a fine instead of imprisonment.

Remission of sentence

## 52. člen

(1) The court may remit the sentence to the perpetrator of a criminal offence where the law specifically so provides.
(2) Where the court has the right to remit the sentence to the perpetrator of a criminal offence, it may mitigate it without the limitations prescribed for mitigation of sentence.

Concurrence of criminal offences

## 53. člen

(1) If the perpetrator has committed two or more criminal offences by one act or by several acts for which he is being tried simultaneously, the court shall first determine the sentence for each individual criminal offence and then impose a single sentence for all those criminal offences.
(2) The court shall impose a single sentence according to the following rules:
1) if it has determined a sentence of life imprisonment for any criminal offence in concurrence, or if it has determined a sentence of thirty years of imprisonment for two or more criminal offences under the second paragraph of Article 46 of this Code in concurrence, it shall impose a single sentence of life imprisonment;
2) if it has determined a sentence of thirty years of imprisonment for any criminal offence in concurrence and the case under point 1) does not apply, it shall impose only that sentence;
3) if it has determined sentences of imprisonment for the criminal offences in concurrence, the single sentence must be greater than each individual determined sentence, but may not reach the sum of the individual sentences and may not exceed thirty years of imprisonment;
4) if sentences of imprisonment of up to one year are prescribed for all the criminal offences in concurrence, the single sentence may not be longer than five years of imprisonment;
5) if it has determined only fines for the criminal offences in concurrence, it shall increase the highest determined fine, which may not exceed the sum of the determined fines and may not exceed three hundred and sixty daily amounts, or if one or more criminal offences were committed out of greed, it may not exceed one thousand five hundred daily amounts;
6) if it has determined a sentence of imprisonment for some criminal offences in concurrence and fines for other criminal offences, it shall impose one sentence of imprisonment and one fine under points 2), 3),
4) and 5) of this paragraph;
7) if it has determined several accessory sentences of the same type for the criminal offences in concurrence, it shall impose a single accessory sentence such that it may not reach their sum and may not exceed the highest general limit of the sentence.
(3) The court shall impose an accessory sentence even if it was determined for only one criminal offence in concurrence; however, if it has determined several fines, it shall impose a single fine under point 5) of the second paragraph of this article.

Continuing criminal offence

## 54. člen

(1) A person who, out of greed or harmful motives, simultaneously or successively commits or attempts to commit two or more identical or similar property criminal offences which, having regard to the place, manner or other identical circumstances, constitute a single activity, commits a continuing criminal offence.

(2) The provisions on concurrence under the preceding article of this Code shall not apply to a continuing criminal offence, but the perpetrator shall be imposed a single sentence for all the criminal offences together within the limits of the sentence prescribed for the most serious criminal offence.
(3) A perpetrator who, by the activity under the first paragraph of this article, together obtains a greater or large property benefit or causes greater or large property damage for which a more severe sentence is prescribed for the criminal offence, shall be imposed that more severe sentence under the second paragraph of this article if his intention was to obtain such benefit or cause such damage by the simultaneously or successively committed criminal offences.

Imposition of sentence on a convicted person

## 55. člen

(1) If the court tries a convicted person for a criminal offence that he committed before he began serving the sentence under a previous conviction, or for a criminal offence that he committed while serving imprisonment, it shall impose a single sentence for all the criminal offences under Article 53; in doing so, it shall take into account that the previously imposed sentence has already been determined. The sentence or part of the sentence that the convicted person has already served shall be credited towards the imposed sentence of imprisonment.
(2) For a criminal offence committed while serving imprisonment, the court shall impose a sentence on the perpetrator irrespective of previously imposed sentences if the unserved part of the previously imposed sentence would be disproportionately small when applying the provisions of Article 53.

Crediting of detention and previous sentence

## 56. člen

(1)	Čas, prestan v priporu, ter kakršen koli odvzem prostosti v zvezi s kaznivim dejanjem, se všteva v izrečeno kazen zapora in denarno kazen.
(2)	Če je uveden kazenski postopek za več kaznivih dejanj in pripor ni odrejen za vsako od njih, se čas, prestan v priporu, všteva v izrečeno kazen zapora in denarno kazen za kaznivo dejanje, za katero je obdolženka oziroma obdolženec (v nadaljnjem besedilu: obdolženec) obsojen.
(3)	Globa, odvzem prostosti ali kakšna druga sankcija, ki jo je obsojenec prestal oziroma plačal za prekršek, ter kazen ali disciplinski odvzem prostosti, ki ga je prestal zaradi kršitve vojaške discipline, se mu všteje v kazen, izrečeno za kaznivo dejanje, katerega znaki imajo tudi znake prekrška oziroma kršitve vojaške discipline.
(4)	Dan pripora, dan odvzema prostosti, dan zapora in dva dnevna zneska denarne kazni ter 42 eurov globe, izrečene za prekršek, so pri vsakem vštevanju izenačeni.

Peto poglavje OPOZORILNE SANKCIJE

1.	Pogojna obsodba

Splošne določbe o pogojni obsodbi

## 57. člen

(1)	Sodišče sme ob pogojih, ki so določeni s tem zakonikom, izreči storilcu kaznivega dejanja pogojno obsodbo namesto kazni.
(2)	S pogojno obsodbo določi sodišče storilcu kaznivega dejanja kazen, ki pa ne bo izrečena, če obsojenec v času, ki ga določi sodišče in ne sme biti manj kot eno leto in ne več kot pet let (preizkusna doba), ne bo storil novega kaznivega dejanja.
(3)	V pogojni obsodbi lahko sodišče določi, da bo določena kazen izrečena tudi, če obsojenec v določenem roku ne vrne premoženjske koristi, do katere je prišel s kaznivim dejanjem, ne povrne škode, ki jo je povzročil s kaznivim dejanjem, ali ne izpolni drugih, v kazenskopravnih določbah predvidenih obveznosti. Rok za izpolnitev teh obveznosti določi sodišče v mejah preizkusne dobe.
(4)	Varnostni ukrepi, izrečeni ob pogojni obsodbi, se izvršijo.

Izrek pogojne obsodbe

## 58. člen

(1)	Pogojna obsodba se sme izreči, če je sodišče storilcu določilo kazen zapora do dveh let ali denarno kazen.
(2)	Pogojna obsodba se ne sme izreči za kazniva dejanja, za katera je predpisana kazen zapora najmanj treh let.
(3)	Sodišče izreče pogojno obsodbo, če glede na osebnost storilca, njegovo prejšnje življenje, njegovo obnašanje po storjenem kaznivem dejanju, stopnjo krivde in glede na druge okoliščine, v katerih je dejanje storil, spozna, da je mogoče pričakovati, da ne bo več ponavljal kaznivih dejanj.
(4)	Če sodišče v pogojni obsodbi določi stranske kazni, sme izreči, da se vse ali posamezne stranske kazni izvršijo.
(5)	Storilcu, ki po zakonu, ki ureja kazenski postopek, prizna krivdo, ko se prvič izjavi o obtožnem aktu, v katerem je za tak primer predlagan izrek pogojne obsodbe, ali jo prizna v sporazumu z državnim tožilcem, sme sodišče izreči pogojno obsodbo tudi za kazniva dejanja, za katera je predpisana kazen zapora najmanj petih let, določiti kazen zapora do petih let, preizkusno dobo pa do desetih let.

Preklic pogojne obsodbe zaradi novega kaznivega dejanja

## 59. člen

(1)	Sodišče prekliče pogojno obsodbo, če stori obsojenec v preizkusni dobi eno ali več kaznivih dejanj, za katera je izreklo kazen zapora dveh let ali daljšo kazen.

(2)	Če stori obsojenec v preizkusni dobi eno ali več kaznivih dejanj, za katera je sodišče določilo kazen zapora manj kot dve leti ali denarno kazen, odloči sodišče, ali bo preklicalo pogojno obsodbo, ko presodi vse okoliščine, ki se nanašajo na storjena kazniva dejanja in storilca, zlasti pa na sorodnost storjenih kaznivih dejanj, njihov pomen in nagibe, iz katerih so bila storjena. Pri tem je vezano na prepoved, da ne sme izreči pogojne obsodbe, če je treba storilcu za kazniva dejanja, ugotovljena v pogojni obsodbi, in za nova kazniva dejanja izreči kazen več kot dveh let zapora (prvi odstavek prejšnjega člena), v primerih priznanj krivde in sporazumov o krivdi pa več kot petih let zapora (peti odstavek prejšnjega člena).
(3)	Če sodišče prekliče pogojno obsodbo, izreče po 53. členu tega zakonika enotno kazen za prej storjeno in novo kaznivo dejanje; pri tem upošteva, da je kazen iz preklicane pogojne obsodbe že določena.
(4)	Če sodišče ne prekliče pogojne obsodbe, sme za novo kaznivo dejanje izreči pogojno obsodbo ali kazen. Če spozna, da je treba tudi za novo kaznivo dejanje izreči pogojno obsodbo, določi po 53. členu tega zakonika enotno kazen za prej storjeno in novo kaznivo dejanje in določi novo preizkusno dobo, ki ne sme biti krajša od enega leta in ne daljša od petih let, v primerih priznanj krivde in sporazumov o krivdi pa ne daljša od desetih let, in se šteje od pravnomočnosti nove sodbe. Obsojencu, ki mu je za novo kaznivo dejanje izrečen zapor, se čas prestajanja te kazni ne šteje v preizkusno dobo, določeno s pogojno obsodbo za prejšnje kaznivo dejanje.

Preklic pogojne obsodbe zaradi prej storjenega kaznivega dejanja

## 60. člen

(1)	Sodišče prekliče pogojno obsodbo, če po njenem izreku ugotovi, da je obsojenec storil kaznivo dejanje, preden je bil pogojno obsojen, in če sodi, da ne bi bilo podlage za pogojno obsodbo, če bi se vedelo za to dejanje. V takem primeru ravna po tretjem odstavku prejšnjega člena.
(2)	Če sodišče ne prekliče pogojne obsodbe, ravna po četrtem odstavku prejšnjega člena.

Preklic pogojne obsodbe zaradi neizpolnitve naloženih obveznosti

## 61. člen

(1)	Če je bilo s pogojno obsodbo obsojencu naloženo, da izpolni kakšno obveznost iz tretjega odstavka 57. člena tega zakonika, pa je ni izpolnil v roku, ki mu je bil določen v sodbi, sme sodišče v mejah preizkusne dobe podaljšati rok za izpolnitev obveznosti ali pa preklicati pogojno obsodbo in izreči kazen, ki je bila določena v pogojni obsodbi. Če spozna, da obsojenec iz upravičenih razlogov ne more izpolniti naložene obveznosti, mu sodišče lahko odpusti njeno izpolnitev ali pa jo nadomesti z drugo ustrezno obveznostjo, določeno v zakonu.
(2)	Če se je v roku za izpolnitev obveznosti iz tretjega odstavka 57. člena tega zakonika, ki je bil obsojencu določen v sodbi, nad njim začel osebni stečaj, se tek roka za izpolnitev te obveznosti za čas trajanja osebnega stečaja prekine, rok, v katerem lahko sodišče sprejme odločitve iz prejšnjega odstavka, pa se ne glede na prejšnji odstavek za čas takšne prekinitve podaljša tudi čez mejo določene preizkusne dobe.

Roki za preklic pogojne obsodbe

## 62. člen

(1)	Pogojna obsodba se sme preklicati v preizkusni dobi. Če stori obsojenec v tem času kaznivo dejanje, ki ima za posledico preklic pogojne obsodbe, pa se to s sodbo ugotovi šele po poteku preizkusne dobe, se sme pogojna obsodba preklicati najpozneje v enem letu po poteku preizkusne dobe.
(2)	Če obsojenec v danem roku ne izpolni obveznosti iz tretjega odstavka 57. člena tega zakonika, sme sodišče najpozneje v enem letu po poteku preizkusne dobe oziroma po poteku roka iz drugega odstavka prejšnjega člena preklicati pogojno obsodbo in izreči kazen, ki je bila določena v pogojni obsodbi.

2.	Pogojna obsodba z varstvenim nadzorstvom

Varstveno nadzorstvo

## 63. člen

(1)	Ob pogojih, določenih v tem zakoniku, sme sodišče določiti, da bo storilec, ki mu je bila izrečena pogojna obsodba, za določen čas med preizkusno dobo pod varstvenim nadzorstvom.
(2)	Varstveno nadzorstvo vključuje z zakonom določeno pomoč, nadzor ali
varstvo.

Pogoji za izrek varstvenega nadzorstva

## 64. člen

(1)	Sodišče izreče ukrep varstvenega nadzorstva, če spozna, da je storilcu med preizkusno dobo potrebna kakšna oblika takega nadzorstva (drugi odstavek prejšnjega člena). Ta ukrep izreče sodišče za določen čas v mejah preizkusne dobe, določene s pogojno obsodbo.
(2)	Če sodišče ugotovi, da varstveno nadzorstvo ni več potrebno, sme izvedbo tega ukrepa ustaviti še pred potekom preizkusne dobe.

## Article 56

(1) Time spent in detention and any deprivation of liberty in connection with a criminal offence shall be credited against the imposed sentence of imprisonment and fine.
(2) If criminal proceedings are instituted for several criminal offences and detention is not ordered for each of them, the time spent in detention shall be credited against the imposed sentence of imprisonment and fine for the criminal offence for which the accused (hereinafter: the accused) is convicted.
(3) A fine, deprivation of liberty or any other sanction which the convicted person has served or paid for a misdemeanour, as well as a sentence or disciplinary deprivation of liberty which he or she has served for a breach of military discipline, shall be credited against the sentence imposed for a criminal offence whose elements also include the elements of a misdemeanour or breach of military discipline.
(4) One day of detention, one day of deprivation of liberty, one day of imprisonment and two daily amounts of a fine, as well as 42 euros of a fine imposed for a misdemeanour, are equated in every crediting.

Chapter Five WARNING SANCTIONS

1. Suspended sentence

General provisions on suspended sentences

## Article 57

(1) Under the conditions laid down in this Code, the court may impose a suspended sentence on the perpetrator of a criminal offence instead of a sentence.
(2) By a suspended sentence, the court determines a sentence for the perpetrator of a criminal offence, which shall not be imposed if the convicted person does not commit a new criminal offence within the time determined by the court, which may not be less than one year and not more than five years (probationary period).
(3) In a suspended sentence, the court may determine that a specified sentence shall also be imposed if the convicted person does not, within a specified time limit, return the pecuniary benefit obtained through the criminal offence, compensate for the damage caused by the criminal offence, or fulfil other obligations provided for in criminal law provisions. The time limit for fulfilling these obligations shall be determined by the court within the limits of the probationary period.
(4) Security measures imposed together with a suspended sentence shall be executed.

Imposition of a suspended sentence

## Article 58

(1) A suspended sentence may be imposed if the court has determined a sentence of imprisonment of up to two years or a fine for the perpetrator.
(2) A suspended sentence may not be imposed for criminal offences for which a sentence of imprisonment of at least three years is prescribed.
(3) The court shall impose a suspended sentence if, having regard to the personality of the perpetrator, his or her previous life, his or her conduct after the commission of the criminal offence, the degree of guilt and other circumstances in which the act was committed, it finds that it can be expected that he or she will not repeat criminal offences.
(4) If the court determines ancillary sentences in a suspended sentence, it may order that all or individual ancillary sentences be executed.
(5) A perpetrator who, under the law governing criminal procedure, admits guilt when first making a statement on the indictment in which the imposition of a suspended sentence is proposed for such a case, or admits it in an agreement with the state prosecutor, may be given a suspended sentence by the court even for criminal offences for which a sentence of imprisonment of at least five years is prescribed, with a sentence of imprisonment of up to five years being determined and a probationary period of up to ten years.

Revocation of a suspended sentence due to a new criminal offence

## Article 59

(1) The court shall revoke a suspended sentence if the convicted person commits one or more criminal offences during the probationary period for which it has imposed a sentence of imprisonment of two years or a longer sentence.

(2) If the convicted person commits one or more criminal offences during the probationary period for which the court has determined a sentence of imprisonment of less than two years or a fine, the court shall decide whether to revoke the suspended sentence after assessing all the circumstances relating to the criminal offences committed and the perpetrator, in particular the similarity of the criminal offences committed, their significance and the motives from which they were committed. In doing so, it is bound by the prohibition that it may not impose a suspended sentence if, for the criminal offences established in the suspended sentence and for the new criminal offences, a sentence of more than two years' imprisonment must be imposed on the perpetrator (first paragraph of the preceding article), or in cases of admissions of guilt and plea agreements more than five years' imprisonment (fifth paragraph of the preceding article).
(3) If the court revokes the suspended sentence, it shall impose a single sentence under Article 53 of this Code for the previously committed and new criminal offence; in doing so, it shall take into account that the sentence from the revoked suspended sentence has already been determined.
(4) If the court does not revoke the suspended sentence, it may impose a suspended sentence or a sentence for the new criminal offence. If it finds that a suspended sentence must also be imposed for the new criminal offence, it shall determine a single sentence under Article 53 of this Code for the previously committed and new criminal offence and determine a new probationary period, which may not be shorter than one year and not longer than five years, or in cases of admissions of guilt and plea agreements not longer than ten years, and shall be counted from the date on which the new judgment becomes final. For a convicted person who is sentenced to imprisonment for a new criminal offence, the time spent serving this sentence shall not be counted in the probationary period determined by the suspended sentence for the previous criminal offence.

Revocation of a suspended sentence due to a previously committed criminal offence

## Article 60

(1) The court shall revoke a suspended sentence if, after its imposition, it establishes that the convicted person committed a criminal offence before being given a suspended sentence, and if it considers that there would have been no basis for a suspended sentence if this act had been known. In such a case, it shall proceed in accordance with the third paragraph of the preceding article.
(2) If the court does not revoke the suspended sentence, it shall proceed in accordance with the fourth paragraph of the preceding article.

Revocation of a suspended sentence due to non-fulfilment of imposed obligations

## Article 61

(1) If the convicted person was required by the suspended sentence to fulfil any obligation under the third paragraph of Article 57 of this Code, but has not fulfilled it within the time limit specified in the judgment, the court may, within the limits of the probationary period, extend the time limit for fulfilment of the obligation or revoke the suspended sentence and impose the sentence that was determined in the suspended sentence. If it finds that the convicted person cannot fulfil the imposed obligation for justified reasons, the court may release him or her from its fulfilment or replace it with another appropriate obligation specified by law.
(2) If, within the time limit for fulfilment of the obligation under the third paragraph of Article 57 of this Code, which was specified for the convicted person in the judgment, personal bankruptcy proceedings have been initiated against him or her, the running of the time limit for fulfilment of this obligation shall be suspended for the duration of the personal bankruptcy, and the time limit within which the court may make the decisions under the preceding paragraph shall, notwithstanding the preceding paragraph, be extended beyond the limit of the specified probationary period for the duration of such suspension.

Time limits for revocation of a suspended sentence

## Article 62

(1) A suspended sentence may be revoked during the probationary period. If the convicted person commits a criminal offence during this time which results in the revocation of the suspended sentence, but this is only established by judgment after the expiry of the probationary period, the suspended sentence may be revoked no later than one year after the expiry of the probationary period.
(2) If the convicted person does not fulfil the obligation under the third paragraph of Article 57 of this Code within the specified time limit, the court may revoke the suspended sentence and impose the sentence that was determined in the suspended sentence no later than one year after the expiry of the probationary period or after the expiry of the time limit under the second paragraph of the preceding article.

2. Suspended sentence with protective supervision

Protective supervision

## Article 63

(1) Under the conditions laid down in this Code, the court may determine that a perpetrator who has been given a suspended sentence shall be under protective supervision for a specified time during the probationary period.
(2) Protective supervision includes assistance, supervision or protection as determined by law.

Conditions for imposition of protective supervision

## Article 64

(1) The court shall impose a measure of protective supervision if it finds that the perpetrator needs some form of such supervision during the probationary period (second paragraph of the preceding article). The court shall impose this measure for a specified time within the limits of the probationary period determined by the suspended sentence.
(2) If the court establishes that protective supervision is no longer necessary, it may stop the execution of this measure before the expiry of the probationary period.

## Article 70

(1) The court may impose one or more security measures on the perpetrator of a criminal offence when the conditions determined by this code are met.
(2) When imposing a security measure, the court shall, according to the principle of proportionality, take into account the gravity of the criminal offence committed and the acts which it reasonably concludes the perpetrator could commit if the security measure were not imposed.

(3) Mandatory psychiatric treatment and custody in a health institution and mandatory psychiatric treatment at liberty shall be imposed independently on a non-accountable perpetrator of an unlawful act if the safety of people cannot otherwise be ensured. In addition to these two measures, the court may also impose a prohibition on practising a profession, revocation of a driving licence and confiscation of objects.
(4) Revocation of a driving licence and confiscation of objects may be imposed if the perpetrator has been sentenced to a punishment, conditional sentence, judicial admonition or if the punishment has been remitted.
(5) A prohibition on practising a profession may be imposed if the perpetrator has been sentenced to imprisonment or if imprisonment has been determined in a conditional sentence.
(6) A prohibition on approaching or communicating with the victim may be imposed if the perpetrator has been sentenced to a punishment, warning sanction or if the punishment has been remitted.

Mandatory psychiatric treatment and custody in a health institution

Article 70.a
(1) The court shall impose mandatory psychiatric treatment and custody in a health institution on a perpetrator who has committed an unlawful act in a state of non-accountability or a criminal offence in a state of substantially diminished accountability and for which a sentence of imprisonment of one year or more may be imposed, if, on the basis of the gravity of the act committed and the degree of the perpetrator's mental disturbance, it determines that at liberty he or she could commit a serious criminal offence against life, body, sexual integrity or property and that such danger can only be eliminated by treatment and custody in a forensic psychiatric ward of a health institution that meets the special security conditions determined by law.
(2) The court shall terminate the measure from the preceding paragraph or replace it with the measure from
Article 70.b of this code when it determines that treatment and custody in a health institution are no longer necessary. After six months have elapsed, the court shall decide each time anew whether further treatment and custody in a health institution are still necessary.

(3) The measure from paragraph one of this article shall last for a non-accountable perpetrator for a maximum of five years.

(4) If a person commits a criminal offence during the serving of a sentence for which the court imposes a security measure in accordance with paragraph one of this article, the serving of the sentence shall be interrupted for as long as the execution of the security measure lasts.
(5) For a perpetrator who has committed a criminal offence in a state of substantially diminished accountability and has been sentenced to imprisonment, the execution of the measure from paragraph one of this article shall be terminated when he or she has spent in the health institution the time for which the sentence was imposed. The time spent in the health institution shall be counted towards the time of serving the sentence. If this time is shorter than the sentence imposed, the court may order that the convicted person must serve the remainder of the sentence or that he or she be released on conditional release. When deciding on the conditional release of a convicted person, the court shall take into account in particular the success of treatment, his or her health condition, the time spent in the health institution and the remainder of the sentence not served.

Mandatory psychiatric treatment at liberty

Article 70.b

(1) The court shall impose mandatory psychiatric treatment at liberty on a perpetrator who has committed an unlawful act in a state of non-accountability if it determines that this is necessary and sufficient to prevent the perpetrator from repeating more serious criminal offences.
(2) The court may also impose mandatory psychiatric treatment at liberty on a perpetrator whose accountability is substantially diminished and who has been released on conditional release pursuant to paragraph five of the preceding article.
(3) Mandatory psychiatric treatment at liberty may last for a maximum of two years. After six months have elapsed, the court shall decide each time anew whether mandatory treatment at liberty is still necessary.
(4) If the perpetrator does not wish to undergo treatment at liberty, or if he or she arbitrarily abandons treatment, or if treatment is not successful, the court may, under the conditions from paragraph one of the preceding article, order that this measure be executed in a health institution. Even in such a case, this measure may last in total for a maximum of two years. After six months have elapsed, the court shall decide again whether this measure is still necessary.

Prohibition on practising a profession

## Article 71

(1) The court may prohibit the perpetrator of a criminal offence from practising a profession, independent activity or any duty if he or she has abused his or her profession, position, activity or duty for a criminal offence and if the court reasonably concludes that it would be dangerous if he or she were to continue practising such activity.
(2) The court shall determine how long the measure from the preceding paragraph shall last; it may not last less than one year and not more than five years, counted from the finality of the decision, whereby the time spent in prison or in a health institution for treatment and custody shall not be counted towards the duration of this measure.
(3) When imposing a conditional sentence, the court may determine that this sentence shall be revoked if the perpetrator violates the prohibition on practising a profession.
(4) The court may decide that this security measure shall cease if two years have elapsed from the commencement of its execution. The court shall decide on this at the request of the convicted person if it determines that the reasons for imposing this measure have ceased.

Prohibition on approaching or communicating with the victim of a criminal offence

Article 71.a
(1) The court may impose on the perpetrator of a criminal offence against life and body, against honour and reputation, against sexual integrity, against human health or another criminal offence with signs of violence a prohibition on approaching or communicating with the victim of any of these criminal offences for a period from one month to three years.
(2) Within the framework of the measure from the preceding paragraph, the court may determine:
- a prohibition on approaching the victim or his or her relatives,
- a prohibition on establishing direct or indirect contacts or communicating with the victim or his or her relatives, including the use of electronic communication means,

- a prohibition on access to individual places where the victim or his or her relatives regularly move, or
- a prohibition on associating with the victim or his or her relatives.
(3) The court may impose this measure if the perpetrator has harmed the physical or mental integrity of the victim by the criminal offence and if it assesses that the perpetrator's contacts or communication with the victim or his or her relatives would pose a danger of repetition of the same type or commission of another criminal offence against the victim or his or her relatives. The court shall select one or more methods of execution of the measure from the preceding paragraph and shall in particular precisely define the persons to whom the measure relates and the relationship between the perpetrator and the victim or his or her relative, appropriate distances of the perpetrator from the victim or his or her relative or places that must be respected, define individual methods of prohibited forms of communication or determine prohibited forms of association.
(4) When imposing a conditional sentence, the court may decide that the sentence shall be revoked if the perpetrator violates the prohibition on approaching or communicating with the victim or his or her relative.
(5) The duration of the prohibition on approaching or communicating shall be counted from the finality of the judgment. The time spent in prison or in a health institution for treatment and custody shall not be counted towards the duration of this measure.
(6) The court may decide that this security measure shall cease if six months have elapsed from the commencement of execution. The court shall decide on this at the request of the convicted person if it determines that the reasons for imposing this measure have ceased.

## 72. člen

(1)	Storilcu kaznivega dejanja zoper varnost javnega prometa sme sodišče odvzeti vozniško dovoljenje za posamezne vrste motornih vozil in pri tem določiti, da se mu ne sme izdati novo dovoljenje za eno do pet let. Če storilec vozniškega dovoljenja nima, sodišče izreče, da se mu dovoljenje ne sme izdati.
(2)	Sodišče sme izreči ta ukrep, če spozna, da bi storilčeva nadaljnja udeležba v javnem prometu pomenila nevarnost za javni promet zaradi njegovega obnašanja, osebnih lastnosti ali nesposobnosti za varno upravljanje motornih vozil.
(3)	Vozniško dovoljenje preneha veljati s pravnomočnostjo sodne odločbe. Čas, prestan v zaporu ali zdravstvenem zavodu za zdravljenje in varstvo, se ne všteva v čas trajanja tega ukrepa.
(4)	Po poteku časa, ki ga je določilo sodišče v okviru najnižje in najvišje mere tega ukrepa, sme storilec na novo pridobiti vozniško dovoljenje ob splošnih pogojih, ki so predpisani za pridobitev posameznih vrst vozniških dovoljenj.
(5)	Sodišče sme odločiti, da ta varnostni ukrep preneha in da sme storilec na novo pridobiti vozniško dovoljenje, če sta potekli dve leti od začetka njegovega izvajanja. O tem odloči sodišče na prošnjo obsojenca, če ugotovi, da so prenehali razlogi za izrek tega ukrepa.

## 73. člen

(1)	Predmeti, ki so bili uporabljeni ali namenjeni za kaznivo dejanje ali so nastali s kaznivim dejanjem, se smejo vzeti, če so storilčeva last.
(2)	Predmeti iz prejšnjega odstavka se smejo vzeti tudi, kadar niso storilčeva last, če to zahteva splošna varnost ali moralni razlogi, vendar pa pravica drugih terjati od storilca odškodnino s tem ni prizadeta.
(3)	Z zakonom se sme določiti obvezen odvzem predmetov, tudi če niso storilčeva

Razlog za odvzem premoženjske koristi

## 74. člen

(1)	Nihče ne more obdržati premoženjske koristi, ki je bila pridobljena s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega.
(2)	Korist iz prejšnjega odstavka tega člena se odvzame s sodno odločbo, s katero je bilo ob pogojih, določenih v tem zakoniku, ugotovljeno kaznivo dejanje.

Način odvzema premoženjske koristi

## 75. člen

(1)	Storilcu ali drugi prejemnici oziroma prejemniku (v nadaljnjem besedilu: prejemnik) koristi se odvzamejo denar, dragocenosti in vsaka druga premoženjska korist, ki je bila pridobljena s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega, če pa mu jih ni mogoče odvzeti, se mu odvzame premoženje, ki ustreza premoženjski koristi.
(2)	Če storilcu ali drugemu prejemniku koristi ni mogoče odvzeti premoženjske koristi ali premoženja, ki ustreza premoženjski koristi, se mu naloži, da mora plačati denarni znesek, ki ustreza tej premoženjski koristi. Sodišče sme v upravičenih primerih dovoliti, da se lahko denarni znesek, ki ustreza premoženjski koristi, plača tudi v obrokih, pri čemer pa rok plačila ne sme biti daljši od dveh let.
(3)	Premoženjska korist, pridobljena s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega, se lahko odvzame tudi tistim, na katere je bila prenesena brezplačno ali za plačilo, ki ne ustreza dejanski vrednosti, če so vedeli ali bi bili mogli vedeti, da je bila pridobljena s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega.
(4)	Če je bila premoženjska korist, pridobljena s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega, prenesena na bližnje sorodnike storilca kaznivega dejanja (razmerja iz 224. člena tega zakonika), ali če je bilo zaradi onemogočanja odvzema premoženjske koristi po prvem odstavku tega člena na te osebe preneseno kakšno drugo njegovo premoženje, se jim odvzame, razen če dokažejo, da so zanj plačali dejansko vrednost.

(5)	Če je premoženjsko korist pridobilo več oseb skupaj, se odvzame vsaki osebi delež, ki ga je pridobila; če se ta delež ne more natančneje ugotoviti, ga določi sodišče ob upoštevanju vseh okoliščin zadeve.

Varstvo oškodovanca

## 76. člen

(1)	Če je bil oškodovancu v kazenskem postopku prisojen premoženjskopravni zahtevek, izreče sodišče odvzem premoženjske koristi, kadar presega oškodovancu prisojeni premoženjskopravni zahtevek.
(2)	Oškodovanec, ki ga je sodišče v kazenskem postopku glede premoženjskopravnega zahtevka napotilo na pravdo, lahko zahteva poplačilo iz odvzete vrednosti, če začne pravdo v šestih mesecih od pravnomočnosti odločbe, s katero je bil napoten na pravdo, in če zahteva poplačilo iz odvzete vrednosti v treh mesecih od pravnomočnosti odločbe, s katero je bil ugotovljen njegov zahtevek.
(3)	Oškodovanec, ki ni prijavil premoženjskopravnega zahtevka v kazenskem postopku, lahko zahteva poplačilo iz odvzete vrednosti, če je pravdo za ugotovitev svojega zahtevka začel v treh mesecih od dne, ko je izvedel za odločbo, s katero je bila odvzeta premoženjska korist, najpozneje pa v dveh letih od pravnomočnosti te odločbe, in če v treh mesecih od pravnomočnosti odločbe, s katero je bil ugotovljen njegov zahtevek, zahteva poplačilo iz odvzete vrednosti.

Odvzem premoženjske koristi pravni osebi

## 77. člen

Če je bila s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega pridobljena premoženjska korist pravni osebi, se ji taka korist odvzame. Pravni osebi se odvzame tudi premoženjska korist ali premoženje, ki ustreza premoženjski koristi, če ga osebe, navedene v prvem odstavku 75. člena tega zakonika, prenesejo nanjo brezplačno ali za plačilo, ki ne ustreza dejanski vrednosti.

Odvzem premoženja zaradi kaznivih dejanj, storjenih v hudodelski združbi

77.a	člen
(1)	Po določbah tega poglavja se odvzame tudi premoženjska korist ali premoženje, ki ga je s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega pridobila ali s katerim razpolaga hudodelska združba.
(2)	Storilcu, ki je storil kaznivo dejanje v hudodelski združbi, se kot premoženjska korist, pridobljena s kaznivim dejanjem, odvzame tudi premoženje, za katero sodišče ugotovi, da izhaja iz kriminalnih dejavnosti, storjenih v tej združbi.

Odvzem premoženja, pridobljenega v zvezi s kaznivim dejanjem

77.b	člen
Po določbah tega poglavja se kot premoženje, pridobljeno v zvezi s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega, odvzame tudi premoženje, ki ga storilec ali druge osebe, ki se jim premoženje odvzame, uporabljajo v svojo izključno ali pretežno korist s privolitvijo oseb, ki jim premoženje pripada, če so te osebe vedele ali bi bile mogle vedeti, da je premoženje pridobljeno s kaznivim dejanjem ali zaradi njega ali da je z njim bilo pripravljeno, storjeno ali prikrito kaznivo dejanje ali da je bilo pridobljeno z namenom, da se uporabi za kaznivo dejanje.

Domneva brezplačnosti

77.c	člen
(1)	Ne glede na pravno podlago prenosa se domneva, da je bila premoženjska korist oziroma premoženje, ki je predmet odvzema po določbah tega poglavja, preneseno brezplačno ali za plačilo, ki ne ustreza dejanski vrednosti, če so jih storilec ali njegovi bližnji sorodniki (razmerja iz 224. člena tega zakonika) neposredno ali posredno prenesli na gospodarsko družbo ali drugo pravno osebo, ki je v njihovi večinski lasti ali imajo v njej pravico izvajati prevladujoč vpliv ali nadzor.
(2)	Družbi ali osebi iz prejšnjega odstavka se premoženjska korist ali premoženje ne odvzame, če dokaže, da je zanj plačala dejansko vrednost.

Osmo poglavje PRAVNE POSLEDICE OBSODBE

Nastanek pravnih posledic obsodbe

## 78. člen

(1)	Obsodbe za posamezna kazniva dejanja ali posamezne kazni imajo lahko za pravno posledico prenehanje oziroma izgubo posameznih pravic ali prepoved pridobitve posameznih pravic.
(2)	Pravne posledice obsodbe ne morejo nastati, če je bila storilcu za kaznivo dejanje izrečena denarna kazen, pogojna obsodba ali sodni opomin ali če mu je bila kazen odpuščena.
(3)	Pravne posledice obsodbe se smejo predpisati samo z zakonom in nastanejo po samem zakonu, s katerim so predpisane.
(4)	Za storilca se sme uporabiti samo tista pravna posledica obsodbe, ki je bila z zakonom določena ob storitvi kaznivega dejanja.

## 72. člen

(1) The court may revoke the driving licence for individual categories of motor vehicles from the perpetrator of a criminal offence against the safety of public traffic and determine that a new licence may not be issued to them for one to five years. If the perpetrator does not have a driving licence, the court shall order that a licence may not be issued to them.
(2) The court may impose this measure if it finds that the perpetrator's continued participation in public traffic would pose a danger to public traffic due to their behaviour, personal characteristics or inability to safely operate motor vehicles.
(3) The driving licence ceases to be valid upon the finality of the court decision. Time spent in prison or a health institution for treatment and care shall not be counted towards the duration of this measure.
(4) After the expiry of the time determined by the court within the minimum and maximum duration of this measure, the perpetrator may obtain a new driving licence under the general conditions prescribed for obtaining individual categories of driving licences.
(5) The court may decide that this security measure shall cease and that the perpetrator may obtain a new driving licence if two years have elapsed from the commencement of its implementation. The court shall decide on this upon the request of the convicted person if it finds that the reasons for imposing this measure have ceased.

Confiscation of objects

## 73. člen

(1) Objects that have been used or intended for a criminal offence or have been created by a criminal offence may be confiscated if they are the property of the perpetrator.
(2) Objects referred to in the preceding paragraph may also be confiscated when they are not the property of the perpetrator if required by public safety or moral reasons, but the right of others to claim compensation from the perpetrator is not affected thereby.
(3) The law may prescribe mandatory confiscation of objects even if they are not the property of the perpetrator.

ODVZEM PREMOŽENJSKE KORISTI, PRIDOBLJENE S KAZNIVIM DEJANJEM

Razlog za odvzem premoženjske koristi

## 74. člen

(1) No one may retain pecuniary gain that has been acquired by or due to a criminal offence.
(2) The gain referred to in the preceding paragraph of this Article shall be confiscated by a court decision by which a criminal offence has been established under the conditions specified in this Code.

Način odvzema premoženjske koristi

## 75. člen

(1) Money, valuables and any other pecuniary gain that has been acquired by or due to a criminal offence shall be confiscated from the perpetrator or other recipient of the gain (hereinafter: recipient), and if it cannot be confiscated from them, property corresponding to the pecuniary gain shall be confiscated from them.
(2) If it is not possible to confiscate the pecuniary gain or property corresponding to the pecuniary gain from the perpetrator or other recipient of the gain, they shall be ordered to pay a monetary amount corresponding to that pecuniary gain. In justified cases, the court may allow the monetary amount corresponding to the pecuniary gain to be paid also in instalments, provided that the payment period may not exceed two years.
(3) Pecuniary gain acquired by or due to a criminal offence may also be confiscated from those to whom it has been transferred free of charge or for payment that does not correspond to the actual value, if they knew or could have known that it was acquired by or due to a criminal offence.
(4) If pecuniary gain acquired by or due to a criminal offence has been transferred to close relatives of the perpetrator of the criminal offence (relationships referred to in Article 224 of this Code), or if any other property of theirs has been transferred to these persons in order to prevent the confiscation of pecuniary gain under the first paragraph of this Article, it shall be confiscated from them unless they prove that they paid the actual value for it.

(5) If pecuniary gain has been acquired by several persons jointly, the share acquired by each person shall be confiscated; if this share cannot be determined more precisely, the court shall determine it taking into account all the circumstances of the case.

Varstvo oškodovanca

## 76. člen

(1) If a property claim has been awarded to the injured party in criminal proceedings, the court shall order the confiscation of pecuniary gain when it exceeds the property claim awarded to the injured party.
(2) An injured party who has been referred by the court to civil proceedings regarding a property claim may request payment from the confiscated value if they commence civil proceedings within six months from the finality of the decision by which they were referred to civil proceedings, and if they request payment from the confiscated value within three months from the finality of the decision by which their claim was established.
(3) An injured party who did not file a property claim in criminal proceedings may request payment from the confiscated value if they commenced civil proceedings to establish their claim within three months from the day they learned of the decision by which the pecuniary gain was confiscated, but no later than two years from the finality of that decision, and if within three months from the finality of the decision by which their claim was established, they request payment from the confiscated value.

Odvzem premoženjske koristi pravni osebi

## 77. člen

If pecuniary gain has been acquired by or due to a criminal offence by a legal person, such gain shall be confiscated from them. Pecuniary gain or property corresponding to the pecuniary gain shall also be confiscated from a legal person if the persons referred to in the first paragraph of Article 75 of this Code transfer it to them free of charge or for payment that does not correspond to the actual value.

Odvzem premoženja zaradi kaznivih dejanj, storjenih v hudodelski združbi

77.a člen
(1) Under the provisions of this chapter, pecuniary gain or property that has been acquired by or due to a criminal offence by a criminal organisation or that is at the disposal of a criminal organisation shall also be confiscated.
(2) Property that the court finds originates from criminal activities committed in that organisation shall also be confiscated from the perpetrator who committed a criminal offence in a criminal organisation as pecuniary gain acquired by a criminal offence.

Odvzem premoženja, pridobljenega v zvezi s kaznivim dejanjem

77.b člen
Under the provisions of this chapter, property that the perpetrator or other persons from whom property is confiscated use for their exclusive or predominant benefit with the consent of the persons to whom the property belongs shall also be confiscated as property acquired in connection with or due to a criminal offence, if those persons knew or could have known that the property was acquired by or due to a criminal offence or that it was used to prepare, commit or conceal a criminal offence or that it was acquired with the intention of using it for a criminal offence.

Domneva brezplačnosti

77.c člen
(1) Regardless of the legal basis of the transfer, it shall be presumed that pecuniary gain or property that is the subject of confiscation under the provisions of this chapter was transferred free of charge or for payment that does not correspond to the actual value if the perpetrator or their close relatives (relationships referred to in Article 224 of this Code) transferred it directly or indirectly to a company or other legal person that is majority-owned by them or in which they have the right to exercise predominant influence or control.
(2) Pecuniary gain or property shall not be confiscated from the company or person referred to in the preceding paragraph if they prove that they paid the actual value for it.

Osmo poglavje PRAVNE POSLEDICE OBSODBE

Nastanek pravnih posledic obsodbe

## 78. člen

(1) Convictions for individual criminal offences or individual sentences may have as a legal consequence the cessation or loss of individual rights or the prohibition of acquiring individual rights.
(2) Legal consequences of conviction cannot arise if a fine, suspended sentence or judicial admonition was imposed on the perpetrator for the criminal offence or if the sentence was remitted.
(3) Legal consequences of conviction may be prescribed only by law and arise by operation of the law by which they are prescribed.
(4) Only those legal consequences of conviction that were determined by law at the time of commission of the criminal offence may be applied to the perpetrator.

## 79. člen

(1)	Pravna posledica obsodbe, ki se nanaša na prenehanje ali izgubo posameznih pravic, je prenehanje opravljanja določenih javnih funkcij ali pooblastil uradne osebe ali prenehanje delovnega razmerja ali izguba pravice tujca do prebivanja v Republiki Sloveniji.

Začetek in trajanje pravnih posledic obsodbe

## 80. člen

(1)	Pravne posledice učinkujejo od dne pravnomočnosti obsodbe.
(2)	Pravne posledice obsodbe, ki so v prepovedi pridobitve posameznih pravic, smejo trajati največ pet let od dne, ko je bila kazen prestana, odpuščena ali zastarana, če ni za posamezne pravne posledice z zakonom določen krajši ali daljši rok.
(3)	Po poteku dveh let od dne, ko je bila kazen prestana, zastarana ali odpuščena, sme sodišče na prošnjo obsojenca odrediti, da preneha pravna posledica obsodbe, ki se nanaša na prepoved pridobitve posamezne pravice.
(4)	Pri presoji, ali naj odredi prenehanje pravne posledice obsodbe, upošteva sodišče vedenje obsojenca po obsodbi, ali je povrnil škodo, ki jo je povzročil s kaznivim dejanjem, in tudi druge okoliščine, ki kažejo, da je prenehanje pravne posledice obsodbe utemeljeno.

Pravni položaj obsojenca po prestani kazni

## 81. člen

(1)	Po prestani, plačani ali na drug način v skladu z zakonom izvršeni, odpuščeni ali zastarani kazni imajo nekdanji obsojenci vse pravice, ki so določene v ustavi, zakonih in drugih predpisih, in lahko pridobivajo vse pravice, razen tistih, ki so jim omejene zaradi izrečenega varnostnega ukrepa ali zaradi nastalih pravnih posledic obsodbe.
(2)	Prejšnji odstavek velja tudi za tiste, ki so na pogojnem odpustu.

Zakonska rehabilitacija in izbris obsodbe

## 82. člen

(1)	Z zakonsko rehabilitacijo se izbriše obsodba iz kazenske evidence in prenehajo vse njene pravne posledice, obsojenec pa velja za neobsojenega.

2)	za pogojno obsodbo – eno leto, od takrat ko je potekla preizkusna doba oziroma rok iz drugega odstavka 61. člena oziroma 67. člena tega zakonika;
3)	za obsodbo na denarno kazen, stransko kazen ali kazen zapora do enega leta – tri leta;
4)	za obsodbo na kazen zapora nad eno leto do treh let – pet let;

Sodna rehabilitacija

## 83. člen

Sodišče sme na prošnjo obsojenca odločiti, da se obsodba izbriše iz kazenske evidence in da obsojenec velja za neobsojenega, če je potekla polovica z zakonom določenega roka, po poteku katerega se obsodba izbriše, če obsojenec v tem času ni storil novega kaznivega dejanja. Pri odločanju o izbrisu upošteva sodišče vedenje obsojenca po prestani kazni, naravo kaznivega dejanja in druge okoliščine, pomembne za izbris obsodbe.

Dajanje podatkov iz kazenske evidence

## 84. člen

(1)	Podatki o izrečenih sodbah se vodijo v kazenskih evidencah. Z zakonom se določita obseg podatkov in dajanje podatkov iz kazenskih evidenc pred izbrisom.
(2)	Na zahtevo vrtcev, varuhov predšolskih otrok, šol, drugih zavodov, ustanov ali društev, ki so jim otroci ali mladoletniki zaupani v učenje, vzgojo, varstvo ali oskrbo, se zaradi

preverjanja izpolnjevanja pogojev za njihovega delavca ali drugo osebo, ki za njih opravlja ali bo opravljala delo, dajo podatki iz kazenskih evidenc tudi za izbrisane obsodbe za kazniva dejanja po 170. členu, po 171. členu, po 172. členu, po 173. členu, po 173.a členu, po drugem odstavku 174. člena, izvršena proti mladoletni osebi, po drugem odstavku 175. člena in po 176. členu tega zakonika ter za izbrisane obsodbe za primerljiva kazniva dejanja, ki jih državljanom Republike Slovenije izrečejo tuja sodišča.
(3)	Z zakonom se določi, da se obsodbe za kazniva dejanja iz prejšnjega odstavka vpišejo v evidenco izbrisanih obsodb za kazniva dejanja zoper spolno nedotakljivost in se predpišejo pogoji, omejitve in postopek za dajanje podatkov o takih obsodbah; v primerih, ki niso zajeti v prejšnjem odstavku, se obsodba kljub ohranitvi v tej evidenci šteje za izbrisano (prvi odstavek tega člena).

Deseto poglavje
TEMELJNE DOLOČBE O IZVRŠEVANJU KAZENSKIH SANKCIJ

Položaj obsojenca na prestajanju kazni zapora

## 85. člen

(1)	Z ustavo in zakoni zajamčene pravice tistih, proti katerim se izvršujejo kazenske sankcije, se smejo v skladu z zakonom odvzeti ali omejiti samo, kolikor je nujno, da se izvrši posamezna kazenska sankcija.
(2)	Oseba, proti kateri se izvršuje kazenska sankcija, ne sme biti mučena in se z njo tudi na drug način ne sme okrutno, nečloveško ali ponižujoče ravnati. Če se je z njo ravnalo tako, ji mora biti zagotovljeno sodno varstvo.
(3)	Z obsojenci je treba ravnati človeško, spoštovati njihovo osebno dostojanstvo ter varovati njihovo telesno in duševno celovitost.
(4)	Obsojencem je treba zagotoviti ustrezno zdravstveno oskrbo, z njihovim soglasjem tudi z zdravljenjem odvisnosti od alkohola ali drog.

## Article 79

(1) The legal consequence of a conviction relating to the termination or loss of individual rights is the termination of the performance of certain public functions or powers of an official person or the termination of employment or the loss of a foreigner's right to residence in the Republic of Slovenia.
(2) Legal consequences consisting of a prohibition on the acquisition of individual rights are:
1) prohibition on the performance of individual public functions or powers of an official person;
2) prohibition on the acquisition of an individual profession or conclusion of an employment contract;
3) prohibition on the acquisition of individual permits or approvals granted by state authorities by their decision.

Commencement and duration of legal consequences of conviction

## Article 80

(1) Legal consequences take effect from the date the conviction becomes final.
(2) Legal consequences of conviction consisting of a prohibition on the acquisition of individual rights may last a maximum of five years from the date the sentence was served, remitted or became time-barred, unless a shorter or longer period is prescribed by law for individual legal consequences.
(3) After the expiry of two years from the date the sentence was served, became time-barred or was remitted, the court may, at the request of the convicted person, order the termination of the legal consequence of conviction relating to the prohibition on the acquisition of an individual right.
(4) In assessing whether to order the termination of the legal consequence of conviction, the court shall take into account the conduct of the convicted person after conviction, whether he has compensated for the damage caused by the criminal offence, and also other circumstances indicating that the termination of the legal consequence of conviction is justified.
(5) The termination of legal consequences of conviction does not affect those rights of others based on the conviction.
(6) Legal consequences cease upon expungement of the conviction.

Chapter Nine
REHABILITATION, EXPUNGEMENT OF CONVICTION AND CONDITIONS FOR PROVIDING DATA FROM THE CRIMINAL RECORD

Legal status of a convicted person after serving the sentence

## Article 81

(1) After a sentence has been served, paid or otherwise executed in accordance with the law, remitted or become time-barred, former convicted persons have all the rights provided for in the constitution, laws and other regulations, and may acquire all rights, except those limited to them due to an imposed security measure or due to legal consequences of conviction that have arisen.
(2) The preceding paragraph also applies to those on parole.

Statutory rehabilitation and expungement of conviction

## Article 82

(1) By statutory rehabilitation, the conviction is expunged from the criminal record and all its legal consequences cease, and the convicted person is deemed unconvicted.
(2) A conviction means a final decision as well as amendments to that decision by amnesty or pardon.
(3) A conviction is expunged from the criminal record within a specified period from the time the sentence was executed, became time-barred or was remitted, if the convicted person does not commit a new criminal offence during that period.
(4) The periods referred to in the preceding paragraph are:
1) for a conviction by which a judicial admonition was imposed on the perpetrator, and for a conviction by which the sentence was remitted – one year from the finality of the court decision;
(2) for a suspended sentence – one year from the expiry of the probationary period or the period referred to in the second paragraph of Article 61 or Article 67 of this Code;
3) for a conviction to a fine, accessory sentence or imprisonment of up to one year – three years;
4) for a conviction to imprisonment of over one year up to three years – five years;
5) for a conviction to imprisonment of over three years up to five years – eight years;
6) for a conviction to imprisonment of over five to ten years – ten years;
7) for a conviction to imprisonment of over ten to fifteen years – fifteen years.

(5) A conviction to imprisonment of over fifteen years is not expunged.
(6) A conviction cannot be expunged from the criminal record while security measures are in force.

(7) A security measure of mandatory psychiatric treatment and care in a health institution and mandatory psychiatric treatment at liberty, which was imposed independently, is expunged three years from the time its execution ceased or the execution became time-barred.

Judicial rehabilitation

## Article 83

The court may, at the request of the convicted person, decide that the conviction be expunged from the criminal record and that the convicted person be deemed unconvicted if half of the period prescribed by law after which the conviction is expunged has elapsed, provided the convicted person has not committed a new criminal offence during that time. In deciding on expungement, the court shall take into account the conduct of the convicted person after serving the sentence, the nature of the criminal offence and other circumstances relevant to the expungement of the conviction.

Providing data from the criminal record

## Article 84

(1) Data on imposed judgments are kept in criminal records. The scope of data and the provision of data from criminal records before expungement are determined by law.
(2) At the request of kindergartens, guardians of preschool children, schools, other institutes, institutions or associations to which children or minors are entrusted for learning, education, care or custody, for the purpose of verifying the fulfilment of conditions for their employee or another person who performs or will perform work for them, data from criminal records shall also be provided for expunged convictions for criminal offences under Article 170, Article 171, Article 172, Article 173, Article 173.a, the second paragraph of Article 174, committed against a minor, the second paragraph of Article 175 and Article 176 of this Code, and for expunged convictions for comparable criminal offences imposed on citizens of the Republic of Slovenia by foreign courts.

(3) The law shall determine that convictions for criminal offences referred to in the preceding paragraph be entered in the register of expunged convictions for criminal offences against sexual integrity and shall prescribe the conditions, limitations and procedure for providing data on such convictions; in cases not covered by the preceding paragraph, the conviction shall be deemed expunged despite being retained in this register (first paragraph of this Article).

Chapter Ten
FUNDAMENTAL PROVISIONS ON THE EXECUTION OF CRIMINAL SANCTIONS

Status of a convicted person serving a prison sentence

## Article 85

(1) The rights guaranteed by the constitution and laws of those against whom criminal sanctions are executed may be withdrawn or restricted in accordance with the law only to the extent necessary to execute an individual criminal sanction.
(2) A person against whom a criminal sanction is being executed must not be tortured and must not otherwise be treated in a cruel, inhuman or degrading manner. If he has been treated in such a manner, judicial protection must be ensured.
(3) Convicted persons must be treated humanely, their personal dignity must be respected and their physical and mental integrity must be protected.
(4) Convicted persons must be provided with appropriate health care, with their consent also including treatment for alcohol or drug addiction.

(4)	Kazen zapora do treh let, razen za kaznivo dejanje zoper spolno nedotakljivost, se za obsojenca, ki izpolnjuje pogoje, določene v zakonu, ki ureja izvrševanje kazenskih sankcij, lahko izvršuje tudi tako, da obsojenec med prestajanjem kazni zapora še naprej dela

ali se izobražuje in prebiva doma, razen v prostih dneh, praviloma ob koncu tedna, ko mora biti v zavodu. Natančnejše pogoje izvrševanja določi zavod.
(5)	Kazen zapora do devetih mesecev se lahko izvršuje tudi s hišnim zaporom, če glede na nevarnost obsojenca, možnost ponovitve dejanja ter osebne, družinske in poklicne razmere obsojenca v času izvrševanja kazni ni potrebe po prestajanju kazni v zavodu ali če je zaradi bolezni, invalidnosti ali ostarelosti obsojenca kazen treba in jo je mogoče izvrševati v ustreznem javnem zavodu.
(6)	V času prestajanja kazni se obsojenec ne sme oddaljiti iz stavbe ali posameznega dela stavbe, kjer se izvršuje hišni zapor, razen če sodišče za določen čas to izjemoma dovoli, kadar je neizogibno potrebno, da si obsojenec zagotovi najnujnejše življenjske potrebščine ali zdravstveno pomoč, ali za opravljanje dela. Sodišče v sodbi, s katero je določilo, da se kazen izvrši s hišnim zaporom, po določbah tega zakonika o pogojni obsodbi določi tudi varstveno nadzorstvo, lahko pa tudi eno ali več navodil. Sodišče lahko obsojencu omeji ali prepove stike z osebami, ki z njim ne prebivajo oziroma ga ne zdravijo ali oskrbujejo in podrobneje določi način izvrševanja hišnega zapora.
(7)	Če se obsojenec brez dovoljenja sodišča oddalji iz stavbe ali posameznega dela stavbe, kjer se izvršuje hišni zapor, ali pa to stori zunaj dovoljenega časa ali ne upošteva omejitve ali prepovedi stikov ali krši druga pravila, ki jih sodišče določi glede izvrševanja hišnega zapora, lahko sodišče s sklepom odloči, da se preostanek izrečene kazni izvrši v zavodu.
(8)	Kazen zapora do dveh let, razen za kaznivo dejanje zoper spolno nedotakljivost, se lahko izvrši tudi tako, da obsojenec namesto kazni zapora opravi v obdobju največ treh let od izvršljivosti sodbe delo v splošno korist. Obseg dela se določi tako, da se en dan zapora nadomesti z dvema urama dela. Organ, pristojen za izvrševanje, pri določitvi dela obsojencu v okviru razpoložljivih del pri izvajalskih organizacijah upošteva obsojenčevo strokovno znanje in sposobnosti, lahko pa tudi tiste njegove nujne interese glede neodložljivih družinskih, izobraževalnih ali poklicnih obveznosti, katerih neupoštevanje bi povzročilo težko popravljivo ali nepopravljivo škodo za uresničevanje teh obveznosti. Delo v splošno korist se opravlja brez nadomestila.
(9)	Sodišče pri odločanju o izvršitvi kazni zapora na način iz prejšnjega odstavka upošteva zlasti vedenje obsojenca v času odločanja, nevarnost ponovitve dejanja na prostosti, možnost in sposobnost za opravljanje primernega dela ter osebne in družinske razmere obsojenca v času predvidenega izvrševanja kazni.
(10)	Sodišče v sodbi, v kateri je določilo, da se kazen izvrši z delom v splošno korist, po določbah tega zakonika o pogojni obsodbi določi tudi varstveno nadzorstvo, lahko pa tudi eno ali več navodil.
(11)	Če obsojenec v celoti ali deloma ne izpolnjuje nalog v okviru dela v splošno korist ali v pomembnem delu ne izpolnjuje navodil v okviru varstvenega nadzorstva ali se izmika stiku s svetovalcem ali drugače krši obveznosti iz dela v splošno korist, sodišče s sklepom odloči, da se izrečena kazen zapora izvrši v obsegu neopravljenega dela.
(12)	O dopustnosti izvršitve kazni zapora na načine, določene s tem členom, odloča sodišče na predlog obdolženca s sodbo, s katero izreče kazen zapora, ali na predlog obsojenca s posebnim sklepom.
(13)	O dopustnosti izvršitve kazni zapora na načine, določene s tem členom, za obdolženca, ki po zakonu, ki ureja kazenski postopek, prizna krivdo, ko se prvič izjavi o obtožnem aktu, v katerem je za tak primer predlagan način izvršitve kazni, ali jo prizna v

sporazumu z državnim tožilcem, sodišče odloči v skladu s tem predlogom oziroma sporazumom.

Način izvršitve denarne kazni

## 87. člen

(1)	Če se denarna kazen ne da niti prisilno izterjati, jo sodišče izvrši tako, da se za vsaka začeta dva dnevna zneska denarne kazni določi en dan zapora, pri čemer zapor ne sme biti daljši od šestih mesecev.
(2)	Če obsojenec plača samo del denarne kazni, se mu ostanek sorazmerno spremeni v zapor, če plača še ostanek, pa se izvrševanje kazni zapora ustavi.
(3)	Po obsojenčevi smrti se denarna kazen ne izvrši.
(4)	Denarna kazen do tristo šestdeset dnevnih zneskov se lahko izvrši tudi tako, da obsojenec v obdobju največ enega leta namesto plačila denarne kazni opravi delo v splošno korist brez nadomestila. Obseg dela se določi tako, da se en dnevni znesek nadomesti z eno uro dela.
(5)	Glede vprašanj, ki niso urejena v prejšnjem odstavku, se smiselno uporabljajo določbe osmega do trinajstega odstavka 86. člena tega zakonika.

Pogojni odpust
translated_text:
## Article 86

(1) Convicted persons serve their prison sentence in institutions for serving sentences (hereinafter: institution), which are determined by law.
(2) Convicted persons are classified into institutions according to how much their freedom must be restricted.
(3) If a convicted person is sentenced to imprisonment of up to five years, the court may order that it be served in an open or semi-open institution or department; if a sentence of imprisonment of up to eight years has been imposed, the court may order that it be served in a semi-open institution or department.
(4) A prison sentence of up to three years, except for a criminal offence against sexual integrity, may also be executed for a convicted person who meets the conditions determined by the law governing the execution of criminal sanctions, in such a way that the convicted person continues to work

or study and reside at home during the serving of the prison sentence, except on days off, usually at the end of the week, when he or she must be in the institution. More detailed conditions of execution shall be determined by the institution.
(5) A prison sentence of up to nine months may also be executed by house arrest if, given the danger of the convicted person, the possibility of repetition of the act and the personal, family and professional circumstances of the convicted person at the time of execution of the sentence, there is no need to serve the sentence in an institution or if, due to illness, disability or old age of the convicted person, the sentence must be and can be executed in an appropriate public institution.
(6) During the serving of the sentence, the convicted person may not leave the building or individual part of the building where the house arrest is being executed, unless the court exceptionally permits this for a specified time when it is unavoidably necessary for the convicted person to secure the most essential necessities of life or medical assistance, or to perform work. The court in the judgment by which it determined that the sentence is to be executed by house arrest, according to the provisions of this code on conditional sentence, shall also determine protective supervision, and may also determine one or more instructions. The court may restrict or prohibit the convicted person from having contact with persons who do not reside with him or her or do not treat or care for him or her and shall determine in more detail the manner of execution of house arrest.
(7) If the convicted person leaves the building or individual part of the building where the house arrest is being executed without the permission of the court, or does so outside the permitted time or does not comply with the restriction or prohibition of contacts or violates other rules determined by the court regarding the execution of house arrest, the court may decide by order that the remainder of the imposed sentence be executed in an institution.
(8) A prison sentence of up to two years, except for a criminal offence against sexual integrity, may also be executed in such a way that the convicted person, instead of imprisonment, performs work in the general interest within a period of at most three years from the enforceability of the judgment. The scope of work is determined so that one day of imprisonment is replaced by two hours of work. The authority responsible for execution, when determining work for the convicted person within the framework of available work at implementing organisations, takes into account the convicted person's professional knowledge and abilities, and may also take into account those urgent interests of his or hers regarding urgent family, educational or professional obligations, the non-observance of which would cause difficult to repair or irreparable damage to the fulfilment of these obligations. Work in the general interest is performed without remuneration.
(9) When deciding on the execution of a prison sentence in the manner from the previous paragraph, the court takes into account in particular the behaviour of the convicted person at the time of decision-making, the danger of repetition of the act at liberty, the possibility and ability to perform appropriate work, and the personal and family circumstances of the convicted person at the time of the anticipated execution of the sentence.
(10) The court in the judgment in which it determined that the sentence is to be executed by work in the general interest, according to the provisions of this code on conditional sentence, shall also determine protective supervision, and may also determine one or more instructions.
(11) If the convicted person does not fully or partially fulfil the tasks within the framework of work in the general interest or does not substantially fulfil the instructions within the framework of protective supervision or evades contact with the counsellor or otherwise violates the obligations from work in the general interest, the court shall decide by order that the imposed prison sentence be executed to the extent of work not performed.
(12) The admissibility of execution of a prison sentence in the manners determined by this Article shall be decided by the court on the proposal of the accused by the judgment by which it imposes the prison sentence, or on the proposal of the convicted person by a special order.
(13) The admissibility of execution of a prison sentence in the manners determined by this Article for an accused who, according to the law governing criminal procedure, admits guilt when first making a statement on the indictment in which a manner of execution of the sentence is proposed for such a case, or admits it in

an agreement with the state prosecutor, shall be decided by the court in accordance with this proposal or agreement.

Manner of execution of fine

## Article 87

(1) If a fine cannot be collected even by force, the court shall execute it by determining one day of imprisonment for every two daily amounts of the fine commenced, whereby the imprisonment may not be longer than six months.
(2) If the convicted person pays only part of the fine, the remainder is proportionally converted into imprisonment for him or her, and if he or she pays the remainder, the execution of the prison sentence is suspended.
(3) After the death of the convicted person, the fine shall not be executed.
(4) A fine of up to three hundred and sixty daily amounts may also be executed in such a way that the convicted person, within a period of at most one year, instead of paying the fine, performs work in the general interest without remuneration. The scope of work is determined so that one daily amount is replaced by one hour of work.
(5) Regarding issues not regulated in the previous paragraph, the provisions of paragraphs eight to thirteen of Article 86 of this code shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Conditional release
